name: Mule Lizard
source: Contact Other Plane: World of the Old Scrolls I
book: Contact Other Plane: World of the Old Scrolls I

facets.bk: Contact Other Plane: World of the Old Scrolls I

body:
XP 400
N Medium animal
Init +1;
Senses low-light vision, scent; Perception +5

DEFENSE

AC 13, touch 11, flat-footed 12 (+1 Dex, +2 natural)
hp 15 (2d8+6)
Fort +6, Ref +4, Will +2

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.

Melee bite -1 (1d8+4)
Space 5 ft.; Reach 5 ft.

STATISTICS

Str 16, Dex 12, Con 16, Int 1, Wis 12, Cha 2
Base Attack +1; CMB +5; CMD 16 (20 vs bull rush and trip)
Feats Endurance
Skills Perception +5, Stealth +5, Survival +5; Racial Modifiers Stealth +4
SQ docile, large mouth, strong-legged

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Docile (Ex)

Unless specifically trained for combat (See the Handle Animal skill) a mule-lizard’s bite is treated as a secondary attack.

Large Mouth (Ex)

The mule-lizard’s large mouth, in proportion to other creatures its size, increases the damage dice it deals by one more than normal.

Strong-legged (Ex)

The mule-lizard is bipedal but has stable, strong legs. They gain a +4 bonus on their CMD vs. bull-rush and trip. Additionally, they may carry loads as if they were a quadruped and may carry riders up to their size.

ECOLOGY

Environment almost anywhere but naturally in swampy areas
Organization solitary, pair or herd (3-10)
Treasure none

This large-headed, bipedal lizard opens its mouth to let out a whiney bleat.

Mule-lizards are extremely adaptable and docile herd lizards. They originated from swampy lands but given their pliability and usefulness as beasts of burden, you can find them anywhere. They adapt to their environment though they are herbivorous, so they have difficulty living in areas without plant life. Their coloration changes to match the terrain around them but not at the same rate as chameleons. It takes them 8 hours to adapt their coloration and during the time of adaption, they lose their bonus to Stealth.
